projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The consistently high presence count (~20) paired with zero camera motion indicates the presence system is likely counting static IoT devices rather than active occupants, which may cause occupancy-based automations to trigger incorrectly.

While presence data confirms ~20 devices are home, the complete lack of camera motion events over 4 hours suggests everyone is stationary indoors rather than moving about as expected. This indicates a quiet, low-activity day suitable for energy optimization, but also warrants a quick check to ensure cameras aren't misconfigured or blanked.

The stable presence count of ~20 devices on a Tuesday morning indicates the household is fully settled at home, suggesting Miller and Penelope are likely home from school today. This may be worth noting if it was an unexpected day off or remote learning day.

The sustained 20-23 device count paired with zero camera motion during weekday evening hours strongly indicates the household (or guests) has settled in for a prolonged stationary activity like a movie night or gaming session, likely in rooms outside camera coverage. This confirms a normal, relaxed evening state rather than an anomaly.

The sustained count of 20-23 'mobile devices' combined with zero camera motion strongly indicates the presence tracker is counting IoT/smart home gadgets rather than people, suggesting the household is likely settled or asleep rather than hosting a large gathering.

The sustained 20-23 device count paired with zero camera motion for over two hours strongly suggests the house is unoccupied with smart devices, tablets, or phones left connected, rather than the family being home and inactive. This persistent pattern warrants a quick verification to confirm occupancy status and prevent unnecessary energy drain.

The highly stable 20-23 device count paired with zero camera motion for over two hours indicates a large, stationary gathering confined to a camera-blind zone, which likely requires temporary network prioritization to prevent congestion.

The sustained count of 20-22 mobile devices paired with zero camera motion over two hours strongly indicates a presence detection anomaly, likely caused by a device stuck in the 'home' state or IoT gadgets being miscounted, rather than a physical gathering. This matters because it could trigger unnecessary automations or mask real activity if the system incorrectly assumes a large crowd is present.

The sustained 20-23 device count paired with zero camera motion over two hours strongly indicates a large gathering in non-camera zones or a persistent network tracking anomaly, warranting a quick check to rule out unauthorized access or device malfunction.

The sustained 20-23 device count paired with zero camera motion indicates a likely gathering or guests occupying camera-blind zones, or cameras being intentionally disabled. This creates a visibility gap during peak occupancy that should be verified against expected household plans.
